SI-4_title.answer: Atypical Brain Asymmetry in Autism -A Candidate for Clinically Meaningful Stratification

DC-1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: EU-AIMS LEAP (European Autism Interventions - A Multicentre Study for Developing New Medications Longitudinal European Autism Project) was used as the primary dataset comprising 352 individuals with autism and 233 neurotypical controls from 5 sites. ABIDE I and II combined dataset (513 individuals with autism and 691 neurotypical subjects from 15 sites) was used as a replication dataset.

The final sample comprised 352 individuals with autism (259 male and 93 female), and 233 neurotypical control subjects (154 male and 79 female) between 6 and 30 years. ... answer.LEAP: normative model training and testing (primary analysis)

DC-2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: EU-AIMS LEAP was used for primary normative modeling analysis - the normative model was trained on the neurotypical cohort (N=233) using 10-fold cross-validation to predict gray matter asymmetry, then applied to individuals with autism. ABIDE I and II combined served as an independent replication dataset to assess replicability of findings.
DC-2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: First, we trained a Gaussian process regression model at each voxel on the neurotypical cohort using age, sex, and site as covariates to predict gray matter asymmetry, resulting in a developmental model of gray matter asymmetry in neurotypical individuals. To avoid overfitting, assess generalizability, and determine whether neurotypical individuals fall within the normative range, we used 10-fold cross-validation in neurotypical individuals before retraining the model in the entire sample to make predictions in individuals with autism. ... To assess replicability, we selected a sample from the publicly available Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) I and II

For the replication analysis, ABIDE I and II combined had 691 neurotypical subjects (473 males and 218 females).
